svg.font-family: DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace
svg.text: $ situc advise example/tcp/tcp.situ
warning: requirement not satisfied
--> example/tcp/tcp.situ:131:8
131 | assert atomic(tcp_header.syn);
| ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ atomic is NonAtomic
--> example/tcp/tcp.situ:41:3
41 | bit syn;
| ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ bit-field applies here
= atomic(tcp_header.syn) is NonAtomic, required AtomicWord
= `atomic` asks that the access fits in a single instruction
= caused by: a bit-packed field -- writing it is a read-modify-write of the containing byte
= 21 other field(s) share this weakness: tcp_header.summed, tcp_header.data_offset, tcp_header.<
reserved0>, tcp_header.cwr, ...
= remedy: widen the field to a whole number of bytes to regain atomic access
5 suggestion(s), highest-yield class first.
option_list.all: put an upper bound on this region
its size is Unbounded, so no caller can size a buffer for the struct that holds it; bound the en
closing frame, or size this from a length field instead of `remaining`
cost: depends on the bound chosen (the bound is the cost, and it is unchosen)
yields: a worst-case extent, so the struct becomes statically allocatable
tcp_header.payload: put an upper bound on this region
its size is Unbounded, so no caller can size a buffer for the struct that holds it; bound the en
